sections.title: Overview
descriptions: On April 17, 2020, American Fork police arrested Cody Greenland near the Target parking lot after responding to a report of a man possibly entering vehicles. The linked news coverage and videos show Greenland kneeling with his hands raised before an officer tackles him from behind. Officers then restrain him and use a Taser.

Greenland later filed a federal civil-rights lawsuit alleging unlawful seizure, excessive force, failure to intervene, and failures in department policies, training, and supervision. All five charges in the related criminal case were dismissed with prejudice on August 5, 2021. The civil lawsuit was settled for an undisclosed amount and dismissed with prejudice on July 21, 2022.

sections.title: Criminal Cases
descriptions: Utah criminal case 201401103 arose from the April 17, 2020 arrest. Greenland was charged with three counts of possession or use of a controlled substance, one count of use or possession of drug paraphernalia, and one count of interference with an arresting officer. Two possession counts were third-degree felonies; the remaining charges were class B misdemeanors.

All five charges were dismissed with prejudice on August 5, 2021. The detailed case history states that the charges were dismissed pending sentencing on other matters. It records scheduled suppression hearings but does not show a ruling granting a motion to suppress.

contents.text_value: Criminal Case History: The detailed XChange history includes the charges, dispositions, hearing minutes, and procedural timeline. Page 14 contains the August 5, 2021 dismissal entry and its reference to sentencing on other matters.

Criminal Case Document Filings: The shorter XChange history lists the charges and dispositions alongside an index of filed documents and court events. It identifies filings available through XChange; it does not contain the underlying filings themselves.

Affidavit of Probable Cause: Caleb Kinnaman’s account of the reported suspicious activity, officers’ efforts to detain Greenland, alleged resistance, and suspected drugs and paraphernalia found during searches. This is the officer’s stated basis for the arrest, rather than a court finding that the allegations were proved.

sections.title: Civil Lawsuit
descriptions: Greenland filed federal case 2:22-cv-00137-RJS on February 28, 2022, against D. T. Cannon, C. Kinnaman, S. Blackburn, Q. Adamson, and American Fork City through its police department. His complaint alleges that officers used excessive force and violated his constitutional rights during the arrest. The attorney planning report states that the defendants denied the allegations and asserted defenses including qualified immunity.

The defendants filed a $25,000 Rule 68 offer of judgment on April 1, 2022. The parties later stipulated to dismissal of all claims with prejudice, and the court entered the dismissal on July 21, 2022. The collected records do not establish that Greenland accepted the April offer or disclose a final settlement amount.

contents.text_value: PACER Court Docket: The filing index and procedural history for the federal lawsuit, from its February 28, 2022 filing through the dismissal entered on July 21, 2022. The final entry states that all claims were dismissed with prejudice and each party would bear its own attorney fees and costs.

Federal Complaint — Document 2: Filed February 28, 2022, the complaint presents Greenland’s account of the encounter and alleged injuries, including a concussion, damaged fingers, ringing in his ears, and PTSD. It sets out claims against the officers and city. These are Greenland’s allegations, rather than findings by the court.

Rule 68 Offer of Judgment — Document 16: Filed April 1, 2022, the defendants offered $25,000, inclusive of damages, costs, interest, and attorney fees, with 14 days to accept. The offer alone does not establish the amount ultimately paid to resolve the lawsuit.

Attorney Planning Meeting Report — Document 17: Filed April 8, 2022, this joint report summarizes the claims and defenses and proposes deadlines and limits for discovery, expert reports, and preparation for trial.

Stipulation of Dismissal With Prejudice — Document 19: Filed July 20, 2022, the parties jointly requested dismissal of the entire lawsuit with prejudice, with each side bearing its own costs and attorney fees. The stipulation does not state a settlement amount or admit liability.

sections.title: News Articles
descriptions: News coverage of Greenland’s arrest and the filing of his federal lawsuit, including body-camera footage and statements from Greenland and his attorney.

contents.text_value: FOX 13 News Utah: Spencer Joseph reports on the lawsuit’s allegations, the body-camera footage, and Greenland’s account of his injuries and the continuing effects of the encounter. The article states that AFPD had not yet responded to the lawsuit at the time of reporting.

sections.title: YouTube Videos
descriptions: Videos presenting footage and commentary about the encounter and subsequent lawsuit. The titles and legal interpretations belong to the respective creators; the court records above document the charges and case outcomes.

contents.text_value: LackLuster: Coverage of the encounter focusing on the officer tackling Greenland from behind while he was kneeling with his hands raised. The video’s title reports that the lawsuit was settled.
Ray Caldwell: A retired police sergeant’s analysis of the body-camera footage, the force used against Greenland, other officers’ responsibility to intervene, and the later civil lawsuit.
Legal Logic: Commentary comparing the body-camera footage with federal excessive-force decisions and discussing Taser use, the duty to intervene, and Greenland’s civil-rights lawsuit.
